nodes.description: The dual-allergen-exposure hypothesis holds that encountering a food allergen across inflamed or barrier-impaired skin (as in atopic dermatitis) primes sensitisation, while the same allergen taken orally promotes tolerance. The outcome is context-dependent: healthy skin promotes tolerance, and only about a third of children with atopic dermatitis go on to a food allergy, so this is a predisposing route rather than a sufficient cause.

evidence.snippet: The dual-allergen exposure hypothesis suggests that impaired skin barrier exposure leads to sensitization, whereas early oral intake induces tolerance.

nodes.description: Ingestion of an intact or partially digested food protein presents that protein to the gut mucosal immune system. A small number of foods account for the great majority of IgE-mediated disease, which is one reason allergen identity rather than diet composition in general is the exposure that matters.

evidence.reference_title: Management of Food Allergies and Food-Related Anaphylaxis.
evidence.snippet: In the US, 9 foods account for more than 90% of IgE-mediated food allergies-crustacean shellfish, dairy, peanut, tree nuts, fin fish, egg, wheat, soy, and sesame.

nodes.description: Introducing an allergenic food by mouth during infancy, rather than delaying it, engages oral tolerance and prevents allergy. In LEAP the protection persisted to age 12, and a pooled LEAP+EAT analysis showed a 75% reduction in peanut allergy; the benefit shrinks the later introduction is delayed, which is the opposite of the predisposing exposure on the skin arm below.

evidence.snippet: An intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis of pooled data showed a 75% reduction in PA (p < .0001) among children randomized to consume peanut from early infancy.

nodes.description: Prompt intramuscular epinephrine, usually by self-injectable autoinjector, is the first-line treatment for food-related anaphylaxis. It does not act on the allergic mechanism upstream of degranulation; it opposes the systemic consequences of mediator release through alpha-1-mediated vasoconstriction and beta-2-mediated bronchodilation.

nodes.description: The default response to a dietary protein is peripheral tolerance, in which a specialised RORgt- and PRDM16-dependent lineage of intestinal antigen-presenting cells drives antigen-specific peripherally induced regulatory T cells. Food allergy begins when this programme is not engaged for a given protein and the response is instead primed toward type 2 immunity. The beta-lactoglobulin ligand-state experiments show that the same protein can take either route: loaded holo-beta-lactoglobulin prevented sensitisation while sustaining regulatory T cells, whereas the ligand-free apo form acted as an allergen -- a demonstration that tolerance versus sensitisation can be decided by the allergen's own loading state rather than by its sequence.

Allergen-specific B cells switch to the IgE isotype and differentiate into IgE-secreting plasma cells. Secreted IgE binds the high-affinity receptor FcepsilonRI on tissue mast cells and circulating basophils, arming them for an allergen-specific response. Sensitisation is clinically silent at this point; the disease becomes manifest only on re-exposure, which is why anaphylaxis is not expected on a genuinely first exposure.

nodes.description: FcepsilonRI signalling triggers calcium influx and exocytosis of preformed granule contents, principally histamine and tryptase, together with newly generated lipid mediators. This is the effector event that produces the clinical reaction, and it is the step whose systemic consequences epinephrine is given to reverse. Serum tryptase released here is also the diagnostic marker of an anaphylactic event.

nodes.description: An allergen bearing two or more IgE epitopes bridges adjacent IgE-FcepsilonRI complexes, and the resulting receptor aggregate initiates signalling. Valency and epitope spacing are not merely permissive: tetravalent antigen produces larger, more complex aggregates and stronger responses than bivalent antigen, can signal at low IgE occupancy, and the geometry of the aggregate determines signalling efficiency. This is the step at which the oligomeric state of the allergen is converted into a quantitative difference in effector output.

evidence.reference_title: IgE Occupancy and Antigen Valency Cooperate to Control FcεRI Aggregation Geometry and Signaling Efficiency.
evidence.snippet: Thus, allergen valency and epitope spatial arrangement dictate FcεRI aggregate organization and subsequent effector cell activation.

evidence.reference_title: IgE Occupancy and Antigen Valency Cooperate to Control FcεRI Aggregation Geometry and Signaling Efficiency.
evidence.snippet: It has been well established that at least two IgE epitopes are required on an allergen to induce effector cell degranulation, and that increases in valency trigger even stronger responses

nodes.description: Many major food allergens are not monomers. Native Ara h 1, the peanut 7S vicilin, assembles into higher-order homo-oligomers (nonamer or decamer), and a truncated 54 kDa isoform lacking the N-terminal domain is instead exclusively trimeric -- which localises the higher-order oligomerisation interface to that N-terminal domain. The cow's milk whey lipocalin beta-lactoglobulin (Bos d 5) likewise associates into dimers in solution. Because oligomerisation multiplies the copies of an epitope carried on one particle, this quaternary structure sets the valency available for downstream FcepsilonRI crosslinking, and the oligomerisation interface is therefore a structural determinant of effector potency rather than an incidental biophysical property. The epitopes must also be *accessible*: in beta-lactoglobulin, occupancy of the lipocalin ligand pocket is predicted to mask major IgE and T-cell epitopes, so the same protein displays different epitope surfaces in its ligand-free and ligand-loaded states.

evidence.snippet: We found that 63 kDa Ara h 1 occurs as higher order homo-oligomeric conformations such as decamer or nonamer, while 54 kDa Ara h 1 occurs exclusively as a homotrimer, indicating that the N-terminal domain of the 63 kDa molecule may be involved in higher order oligomerization.

nodes.description: Omalizumab is an anti-IgE monoclonal antibody, FDA-approved for reducing allergic reactions to foods in patients with one or more food allergies. It sequesters free IgE so that less is available to arm FcepsilonRI on mast cells and basophils, raising the reaction threshold across multiple foods at once. Like oral immunotherapy it raises the threshold rather than curing, and patients continue to avoid the culprit foods and carry epinephrine.

evidence.reference_title: Omalizumab for the Treatment of Multiple Food Allergies.
evidence.snippet: A total of 79 of the 118 participants (67%) receiving omalizumab met the primary end-point criteria, as compared with 4 of the 59 participants (7%) receiving placebo (P<0.001).

nodes.description: Escalating-dose oral immunotherapy with a characterised peanut protein product, FDA-approved for peanut allergy. It raises the dose tolerated at challenge and reduces symptom severity on exposure, but it is an adjunct to avoidance and epinephrine rather than a replacement: it desensitises rather than curing, and patients continue to carry epinephrine.

evidence.reference_title: AR101 Oral Immunotherapy for Peanut Allergy.
evidence.snippet: AR101 resulted in higher doses of peanut protein that could be ingested without dose-limiting symptoms and in lower symptom severity during peanut exposure at the exit food challenge than placebo.

nodes.description: The allergen-specific CD4 T cell response is redirected toward a T-helper 2 programme, with group 2 innate lymphoid cells contributing innate type 2 cytokine production. IL-4 and IL-13 from this compartment are the signals that license the B cell switch to IgE, making this the step at which a tolerogenic response is converted into a sensitising one.
